title: Telemetry-driven adaptive prefill router with kernel-confidence scoring and regret-based fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a telemetry-driven adaptive router that selects speculative prefill/decode candidates using per-kernel confidence scores, continuous calibration over sliding windows, and a regret-based fallback policy. Goal is to increase fast-path acceptance while bounding user-visible latency and token cost regressions.
background: We currently have multiple prototype strategies for speculative decode routing (prefill probes, staged fallbacks, and kernel-aware heuristics). Engineering and perf teams lack a single telemetry surface and decision module that (1) derives confidence signals per kernel/model variant, (2) adapts thresholds in production based on observed acceptance/regret, and (3) executes safe fallbacks with minimal tail latency impact.
proposed_solution: Design and implement a router component that consumes streaming decode telemetry (early-token match scores, kernel execution fingerprints, softmax-entropy proxies, per-kernel latency distributions) and computes a lightweight kernel-confidence score for each spec candidate. The router will: 1) compute an acceptance threshold using an exponential moving average of recent acceptance rate and regret; 2) prefer candidates with higher kernel-confidence and cost-efficiency score; 3) trigger fallback when confidence drops below a dynamic threshold or when probe outcomes indicate degraded acceptance; 4) emit structured telemetry for offline calibration and A/B evaluation. The implementation will be modular (router + telemetry adapter + simulation harness) so teams can iterate policies without changing runtime kernels.
acceptance_criteria: Router produces per-request kernel-confidence values and logs them to structured telemetry (JSON) for every speculative attempt
E2E A/B experiment shows at least 12% increase in fast-path acceptance for conversational workloads without increasing 95th percentile latency by more than 5%
Fallback latency median and 95th percentile remain at or below current baseline under bursty workload simulations
Simulation harness reproduces production traffic patterns and exposes estimated token-cost delta and regret metric per policy variant
Automated alerts exist for >3% daily increase in observed regret compared to baseline for a given model family
tasks: Design: define kernel-confidence formula (components: early-token similarity, softmax entropy proxy, kernel fingerprint stability, historical acceptance rate)
Infra: extend decode telemetry pipeline to include kernel fingerprints and early-token match scores (PR: github.com/redwood/infra/telemetry#1234)
Runtime: implement router shim that queries kernel-confidence and applies dynamic thresholding (feature-flag behind runtime-1.22)
Simulations: build a traffic generator to replay real prefix distributions and measure regret/cost for policy variants
Dashboards: add per-model/per-kernel confidence heatmap and daily regret trend to Console
Safety: integrate canary rollout with circuit-breaker that disables speculative routing if fallback ratio exceeds threshold
Docs: write design doc and operator runbook with rollback steps and known limitations
rollout_plan: Internally gated: land telemetry + router behind feature-flag on staging (week 1)
Canary: enable on 5% of traffic for conversational workloads with strict monitoring (week 2)
Experiment: run A/B test against control for two weeks to compute acceptance and regret metrics (week 3-4)
Gradual increase: expand to 25% then 100% for traffic segments that meet safety checks (weeks 5-7)
Fallback: automatic disable if daily regret delta > 3% or if 95th latency exceeds baseline by configured margin
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: miscalibrated confidence leads to increased user-visible errors. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, short canaries, and automatic rollback on regret spikes
Risk: additional telemetry increases cost and storage. Mitigation: sample at configurable rate and compact confidence records (aggregates for older windows)
Risk: false positives from kernel fingerprint noise causing unwarranted fallbacks. Mitigation: incorporate stability smoothing and require multiple consecutive low-confidence probes before fallback
Risk: coordination overhead between runtime and infra teams. Mitigation: clear API contract for telemetry adapter and weekly syncs during rollout
notes: Prototype experiments from Jan show kernel-fingerprint correlated with early acceptance on Llama2-70B family (Spearman rho ~0.42)
We will reuse the existing prefill probe path for early-token scoring to avoid new RPCs in hot path
Consider extension: cost-aware routing weight that penalizes high-cost quantized kernels only when their confidence advantage is marginal
